chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us in Nahawand in the year 273 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the year 229 AH, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I was with Ja'far ibn Muhammad in a mosque in Mecca, and he was holding my hand, so he said: 'O Abban, Allah will bring three hundred and thirteen men to this mosque of yours. The people of Mecca will know that their fathers and grandfathers have not yet been created. They will have swords on them, and on each sword is written the name of the man, his father's name, his appearance, and his lineage. Then a caller will be commanded to call out: 'This is al-Mahdi. He judges with the judgments of David and Solomon, and he is not asked to provide evidence for that.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the 313 men coming to Mecca with al-Mahdi according to the hadith of Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Ja'far al-Sadiq (as) highlights the eschatological sign of 313 men whose ancestors are yet unborn, emphasizing the miraculous nature of the Mahdi's army. Their leader will exercise divine authority in judgment, akin to David and Solomon, requiring no further proof, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology regarding the establishment of global justice.
